Class IoRuntime

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime.IoRuntime
public final class IoRuntime extends Object
Hardware calls that wait without holding up the other threads. The runtime is never preempted part-way, so a library loop that waits on a device (delay(1) until a response arrives) used to stall every thread for as long as it waited. Such loops call juno_io_wait instead: with threads it sleeps the calling thread, so the others run meanwhile; without threads it is the plain delay it replaced.

A thread that sleeps inside a library call can find another thread entering the same library, which none of the Arduino libraries tolerate halfway through a transaction. So each waiting entry point holds a device guard (JunoIoGuard) for its whole call: a second thread waits its turn, like a synchronized method, while threads that do not touch the device keep running. HTTP requests instead use core-bounded, independently owned JunoHttpGuard leases: two on R4/Q and one on WiFi Rev2, whose blocking TLS handshake can starve another response. Wi-Fi setup and the HTTP server retain the exclusive network guard. A guard records its owner; cancelling a structured subtask that owns one runs the guard's abort hook (closing a half-used client) and releases it, so the device does not stay locked by a thread that will never run again.

Some waits happen inside a vendor library, out of the shim's reach. Where the core has an RTOS (the UNO Q's Zephyr, whose network calls all wait on Linux through Arduino_RouterBridge), such a call runs on an I/O worker thread while its caller is parked in the scheduler (juno_io_offload); elsewhere it still holds every thread.
